faq_entries.question: How do I apply for a place?
faq_entries.answer: Start by registering your interest, then complete the multi-step application form on the Admissions page. We'll confirm receipt, arrange an entry assessment where relevant, and follow up with next steps.

faq_entries.question: Is there an entry assessment?
faq_entries.answer: Yes — a short, age-appropriate assessment helps us understand where your child is and how best to support them from day one. Details are shared once your application is received.

faq_entries.question: Is this the full British curriculum?
faq_entries.answer: Yes, taught live by qualified UK teachers, alongside a dedicated Islamic Studies programme, through to GCSE at Year 10–11.

faq_entries.question: What equipment does my child need?
faq_entries.answer: A reliable internet connection and a laptop or tablet with a camera and microphone. Full technical requirements are confirmed ahead of the January 2027 launch.

faq_entries.question: How is Qur'an memorisation (hifz) taught?
faq_entries.answer: Hifz sits alongside academic subjects as a first-class part of the timetable, with progress tracked just as academic subjects are.

faq_entries.question: Do you support children with additional needs?
faq_entries.answer: We aim to support a range of additional needs within our online setting. Please tell us about your child's needs during the application so we can discuss what's possible together.

faq_entries.question: What year groups do you accept?
faq_entries.answer: We accept children from Reception through to Year 11 — Early Years and Key Stage 1 through to GCSE (Key Stage 4).

faq_entries.question: When does Tarbiyyah Global Academy launch, and can I apply now?
faq_entries.answer: Live lessons launch in January 2027. Applications are open now — you can register your interest or start the full application at any time before then.

faq_entries.question: What's the difference between registering interest and applying?
faq_entries.answer: Registering interest is a short, no-obligation form so we can keep you updated as places open. Applying is the full multi-step application, including your child's year group, and starts the formal admissions process.

faq_entries.question: Can my family apply from outside the UK?
faq_entries.answer: Yes. Tarbiyyah Global Academy is an online school for families anywhere in the world, bringing the same ethos and standard of care as our established UK schools to wherever home is.

faq_entries.question: What does the published fee include, and what's billed separately?
faq_entries.answer: The published fee covers tuition for the relevant year group band. GCSE exam entry fees (Year 10–11) are billed separately by the exam centre and are not included in tuition fees.

faq_entries.question: Are fees inclusive of VAT?
faq_entries.answer: Yes — every figure on our Fees page is inclusive of 20% VAT, so there's nothing extra added on top of the published price.

faq_entries.question: What happens if I need to withdraw, or a payment is missed?
faq_entries.answer: Our Fees Policy, published on the Policies page, sets out payment terms, refunds and what happens if a payment is missed — please read it before enrolling.

faq_entries.question: How do I actually pay fees?
faq_entries.answer: Fees can be paid by bank transfer or card. Full payment instructions are shared once a place is offered.

faq_entries.question: What year groups and key stages do you cover?
faq_entries.answer: Reception and Key Stage 1 (Reception–Year 2), Key Stage 2 (Year 3–6), Key Stage 3 (Year 7–9), and Key Stage 4/GCSE (Year 10–11) — see our Curriculum page for the full subject list and a sample week at each stage.

faq_entries.question: Do you teach GCSEs?
faq_entries.answer: Yes. Year 10–11 follow live, GCSE-specification lessons across core and options subjects. GCSE exam entry fees are billed separately by the exam centre.

faq_entries.question: What does a typical school week look like?
faq_entries.answer: A live-timetabled mix of academic subjects, Islamic Studies, Qur'an and Arabic, with independent work and PE/wellbeing time built in — see the sample week on each key stage's curriculum page.

faq_entries.question: Can we choose our timetable?
faq_entries.answer: Yes. Choose a Standard Monday–Friday timetable, mirroring a traditional school week, or an Intensive Monday–Thursday timetable with independent Friday set aside for catch-up, Qur'an practice or family time.

faq_entries.question: Will my child be in front of a screen all day?
faq_entries.answer: No. Lessons are structured with regular breaks, offline and hands-on activities, and independent work that doesn't require a device, so learning stays healthy and sustainable.

faq_entries.question: Will there be a separate parent/student portal to log into?
faq_entries.answer: Lessons, homework, attendance and reports will live in our own Learning Platform, built directly into this website — no separate system to set up. This is being finalised ahead of the January 2027 launch.

faq_entries.question: Is Qur'an memorisation (hifz) part of the curriculum at every stage?
faq_entries.answer: Yes — Qur'an & Hifz appears as a subject on the timetable at every key stage, from Reception through to GCSE, alongside academic subjects.

faq_entries.question: Is Arabic taught, and is it compulsory?
faq_entries.answer: Yes, Arabic is taught as a timetabled subject at every key stage, from Reception through to Year 11.

faq_entries.question: How does Islamic Studies fit alongside the British curriculum?
faq_entries.answer: Islamic Studies, Qur'an and Arabic are taught on the timetable at every key stage, alongside the full British curriculum through to GCSE — not as an after-school extra.

faq_entries.question: Do you have a SEND policy?
faq_entries.answer: Yes — our SEND and Inclusion Policy is published in full on the Policies page, alongside our Equality, Diversity and Accessibility Policy.

faq_entries.question: Can I discuss my child's needs before applying?
faq_entries.answer: Yes — contact us any time before or during your application to talk through what support might look like for your child.

faq_entries.question: What should I include in my application about my child's needs?
faq_entries.answer: Please tell us about your child's needs in the application's notes section (or get in touch beforehand) so we can discuss what's possible together ahead of any entry assessment.

faq_entries.question: What does the application fee cover?
faq_entries.answer: The {{applicationFee}} application fee is non-refundable and covers the baseline assessment and administrative review. It is separate from the one-time {{registrationFee}} registration fee, which is payable on acceptance of a place and no later than 19 December 2026.

faq_entries.question: Can I pay fees monthly?
faq_entries.answer: Yes. Fees are for the shortened January–July 2027 period. You can pay annually (with a {{annualDiscount}} discount if paid in full by 19 December 2026), termly ({{terms}} payments) or monthly ({{instalments}} payments) for every year group band. The instalments always add up exactly to the annual fee — see the Fees page for the full table and payment dates.

faq_entries.question: What happens after I submit my application?
faq_entries.answer: We confirm receipt and review your application, then arrange a supervised online assessment and an interview with you and your child. If we offer a place, we email the offer; it is confirmed once we receive proof of the application fee (if unpaid), the {{registrationFee}} registration fee and your first payment.
